tagline: Follow the bluffs, the river towns, and the long autumn views.
intro: The Great River Road follows the Mississippi from Minnesota to the Gulf through ten states. This story covers its Wisconsin section, which runs along the east bank on Highway 35 from Prescott in the north to the Illinois line.

On the Wisconsin side the road sits between steep limestone bluffs and the river's backwaters, passing through a chain of old river towns. Lake Pepin, a natural widening of the Mississippi, is the broadest water along the way.
season: Late September into October for fall colour. Summer for river towns in full swing.

moments.title: Lake Pepin
moments.text: The river spreads into a lake several miles wide. Pull-offs near Maiden Rock and Stockholm look straight across it.

moments.title: Alma
moments.text: A narrow town squeezed between the bluff and the river, with a lock and dam at its edge.

moments.title: Perrot State Park
moments.text: Trails near Trempealeau climb the bluffs above the confluence of the Trempealeau and Mississippi rivers.

moments.title: Prairie du Chien
moments.text: One of the oldest European settlements on the upper Mississippi, near where the Wisconsin River meets it.

practical: WisDOT describes the Wisconsin section as 250 miles along WIS 35. The mapped segments in the national dataset total a little less.
Distances shown here are totals of the mapped road segments in the national dataset, not a suggested itinerary.
Directions go to the start of the Wisconsin section. Rambleroo does not route along the byway itself.
